I'm an amateur web designer with nothing to do, so I made this guide based off the experience I acquired doing the CSS for /v/pcmasterrace. This guide will demonstrate how Voat is structured, and how you can manipulate it's structure to make your subverse look unique. I'm assuming you have a basic understanding of CSS and HTML at worse.

The first thing you need to know is the basic layout of a subverse. Familiarize yourself with this template, which shows the hierarchy of html containers that make up the general structure of the site. We will be going over each one individually, as well as it's relevant children and descendants.

*

The asterisk rule denotes the universal selector. Any declaration it sets will be used for every element unless that element specifies it's own. Adding !important to a declaration makes that declaration the one used even if an element specifies it's own. For example, if you wanted every background to be red, you could add this to your stylesheet:

* { background: red !important; }

It is a good way to set the webpage's primary font, but it's probably best to avoid using it for most things (don't use it to set something like margin or padding).

body

As you should already know, body contains every part of a webpage, it is at the top of the hierarchy. It isn't the same as the universal selector though, it is simply a container and acts as every container's parent. If you wanted to put a border around the webpage, or set it's background, you would do it here.

#header

The #header div contains the bar at the top of the page with links to your subscribed subverses, and the bar with Voat's logo on it. Most people set it's background to act as a banner, and set it's height to the size of the banner. You can find a guide on how to implement your own banner here.

#sr-header-area

This is the bar at the top of the webpage with all of your subverses. The CSS under it is rather obfuscated in my opinion, and it took me a while to get it right for /v/pcmasterrace. Note that .flat-list is used multiple times.

#header-container

This is the bar with The Voat logo on it. It spans across the entire page, and only has one child, #header-banner, which contains all of the buttons and account info. If you want #header-banners content to span across the page set the max-width in #header-container to 100%.

#header-banner

This contains the Voat logo, page name, hot/new/top buttons, share a link and discuss buttons, and account information. Beware changing anything on this as Voat uses media queries to make it look completely different at low resolutions. They start at 950px wide, as well as 870px, 750px, and 700px. Here are it's relavant children:

  • #header-img: The Voat logo. You can change this to a unique logo for your subverse. There's a good guide on how to do that here.

  • .pagename a: The name of your subverse. You can change it's text to whatever you want with this guide. There's an easy way to make this act as your banner. I'll post a guide on how to do that in the future and edit this.

  • .tabmenu: Contains the 5 buttons.

  • #header-account: Contains your login information. Note that it's child changes from .logged-in to .logged-out depending on whether or not you are logged in.

#container

This contains all of the posts, as well as the side bar. Making it's max-width set to 100% wide will make posts stretch across the entire webpage to the side bar. For whatever reason, (as of the time writing this) your custom CSS is under this. If you want to modify or look at someone's CSS without permanently changing it you'll want to do it there.

#container > .content

This contains the posts. The reason I used the #container > selector is because the class is used elsewhere (on the side bar, for some reason), so you have to use it if you only want to effect this usage of the class. You should note that the right side margin has to account for the side bar, so if you change the size of the sidebar you need to change it.

.submission

This contains posts. Changing .submission will change the style of every post, but you can also use .even and .odd to specify certain styles for every other post. There's also .stickied for sticky posts. The voting buttons are images from a sprite sheet. I reccomend you use this guide to learn how to change them rather then try to figure it out on your own. Relevant descendants:

  • .scorebar: The bar next to a post that denotes it's upvoat/downvoat ratio. Use .scorebar-likes and .scorebar-dislikes to change the colors used.

  • a.title.may-blank: The post titles. You should use :visited and even :hover pseudo classes to make it's color change based on whether you've visited them or are hovering over them with your cursor.

.side

The side bar. Note that the it is hidden under 870px wide, so correct any changes to it with media queries so that the subverse is usable under mobile. You should also note that it uses .md for you sidebar text, the same class used for comments. So if you don't specify, it will use the same styling you use for comment formatting.

.footer-container

The page footer. Rather boring, except for .footer which contains the footer's text. If you are making your own custom theme, you might want to add this to give yourself some credit:

.footer:before { content:"Theme by [@usernamehere](https://preview.voat.co/user/usernamehere)"; }

Here are some other random useful peices of information you should know.

  • Night mode support

You should make an effort to support night mode, it isn't hard and will please your subscribers. Please don't force one mode or disregard users of a mode. The way you implement mode specific CSS is simple, just put .light or .dark in front of your rule. The body is changed depending on your mode, from body.light to body.dark. The following example will demonstrate how to do this.

.light a {
 color: black;
}
.dark a {
 color: white;
}
  • resolution support

Please also make an effort to support all common resolutions, from mobile to 4k. This means you're likely going to have to use media queries in lots of places. Have a method of making your banner look good at any resolution, whether that means making it 4096px wide or making it fade, etc...

Note: I will be continuously editing this guide to add more information, It is somewhat lacking right now. If I got something wrong don't hesitate to comment telling me.
